clinician.trajectory_summary: A 74-year-old male presented in 2005 with a one-year history of pruritic cutaneous lesions on his left lower extremity. Physical examination revealed an erythematous plaque and cord-like nodular lesions on the left thigh and leg. Initial workup including culture, histopathological, and mycological examinations was performed, but the patient was subsequently lost to follow-up. The patient returned in 2017 with progressive disease characterized by ulcers with perilesional induration, erythema, and desquamation on the left leg, along with cord-like, firm, brown nodules along the medial aspect of his left thigh and leg. Histopathological examination of skin lesions demonstrated round yeasts with thick double walls occurring singly or in chains connected by tubular projections on Grocott's methenamine silver stain, establishing the diagnosis of lobomycosis.
